text.p: These are the leading stories in the Angolan press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Mininster Franca Van Dunem held brief talks with a visiting delegation from U.S. oil company Texaco.

- United Nations special envoy to Angola, on a whirlwind tour of some southern African countries and Gabon, said on a stopover in Luanda on Thursday that the heads pf state for Namibia, Zimbabwe and Zambia had expressed their support to help Angola's peaceful transition from two decades of war.

- Up to 10,982 former rebel UNITA soldiers have so far been selected for a single Angolan army, the U.N. said. The government and UNITA agreed to integrate a total of 26,300 UNITA soldiers into a post war unified military.
- The Luanda provincial government is considering a plan to build a hotel on the site of the capital's zoo which was closed during the war and the animals shipped to South Africa.
